summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Futoshi Takehashi studied at Otani University (attested 1992) and held an assistant post at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo works in Tibetology and religious studies. A PhD student at the University of Cambridge under Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026), Luo also holds a post at Cambridge.

Fyodor Buslaev worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov at Moscow State University (1834–1843), where he later served on the faculty, becoming an Adjunkt in 1850.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the universities of Vienna and Bonn under Minaev, Oldenburg, Jagić, Bühler, and Jacobi, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg (1901–1930).

Félicien de Saulcy worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École polytechnique (1826–1828), the École d'application de l'artillerie et du génie in Metz (1828–1830), and under Eugène Burnouf.

Félix Lacôte was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Paris studying under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at EPHE (1904–1905) and as professor at the University of Lyon from 1911.

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven, Bonn, Munich, and Paris under Burnouf, Lassen, and Thiersch. He served as an extraordinary (1845) and ordinary professor (1853–1877) at KU Leuven.

An Indologist and linguist, G. B. Beaman earned a B.A. from the University of Cincinnati (~1889–1893), studied at the University of Jena (1893), and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (1894–1895) under Ernst Windisch.

G. B. Palsule was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
G. Herberich was an Indology scholar who studied under Julius Jolly and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Würzburg by 1893.
G. K. Jenkins worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Bloxham School and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of London and SOAS, studying under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, and served as lecturer and dean at the University of Ceylon.

G. Rita Dudley-Grant, active in Buddhist studies, trained in physiotherapy at NHS Grampian (1983–1986) and Robert Gordon University (1994–1997). She held posts at Virgin Islands Behavioral Sciences (attested 2003) and NHS Grampian (2004).

G. S. Sahay worked in Indology and philosophy, serving as research officer at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005). He studied at the University of Nebraska Medical Center and held posts at MIT and Oregon State University.
G. Srinivasa Murti worked in Indology and served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

G. Thomas Tanselle earned his bachelor's from Yale (~1951–1955). He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006).
G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004).

G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant for the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and retired from the office of the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Gabriel Engelsmann was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1881–1885).
